frequency_question: What proportion of complex bilateral water treaty renewals or drafting cycles complete all required technical harmonization and administrative signing steps within a 64-day terminal window?
membership_rule: Includes all documented transboundary water treaty renegotiation processes or major operational protocol drafting cycles between sovereign states where a strict administrative timeline was imposed. Excludes domestic water management agreements.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Permanent Indus Commission annual meetings and protocol renewals
Ganga Water Sharing Treaty initial 1996 drafting and technical annexure finalization
Mahakali Treaty supplementary exchange of letters and joint project finalizations
Teesta River interim water sharing draft finalization attempts

provenance_note: claimed 1 hits but 2 of 4 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 4 representative transboundary hydro-diplomacy drafting cycles examined; 1 completed within a compressed timeline, 3 experienced administrative or technical delays exceeding 64 days.
known_gaps: Bilateral negotiations often experience classified internal inter-ministerial delays that are not fully captured in public administrative histories.
skeleton: Treaty renewal cycles requiring joint scientific data collection (30 days), draft text harmonization across ministries (30 days), and cabinet/executive sign-off procedures (14 days), evaluated against a strict 64-day calendar window.
multiplier: 3 phases of sequential administrative friction totaling a minimum baseline duration of 74 days versus 64 available days.
validity_reason: Bureaucratic processing speeds and inter-ministerial clearance protocols for transboundary treaties remain stable across multi-decade windows.
